neighbours.label: granting someone freedom from supervision or restraint ('more freedom', 'left alone', 'released', 'let them have')
fire: As your daughter matures, you can slowly hand her more freedom with her weekends.
My aunt would not allow the toddler to be left alone near the pool.
The court agreed that the defendant could be released while awaiting his appeal.
Should we let our twelve-year-old have a bank card of her own?
The warden granted the prisoner his freedom after twenty years behind bars.
Employers who give staff more autonomy and freedom find they stay longer.
He thinks they should never let anyone with a record have a gun.
The nurse said the patient was free to go home on his own after lunch.
quiet: As your daughter matures, you can slowly hand her more homework for her weekends.
My aunt would not allow the toddler to be fed peanuts near the pool.
The court agreed that the defendant should be jailed while awaiting his appeal.
Should we buy our twelve-year-old a new coat of her own?
The warden sentenced the prisoner to solitary after twenty years behind bars.
Employers who give staff more training and pay find they stay longer.
He thinks they should always check anyone with a record for a job.
The nurse said the patient was ready for his second dose after lunch.

notes: Card: ' freedom' x4, ' free', ' released', ' alone', ' let'; promotes ' without', ' freedom', ' granted'. Probe: 'more freedom' 0.639; 'left alone' 0.493; 'released on bail' 0.813; 'more chores' 0.126; 'held in custody' 0.054; 'freedom of the press' 0.122, so political freedom is weak. Near misses keep the sentence and drop the grant.
